newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: BIS web site expands with central bank speeches.
newsitem.headline: BIS web site expands with central bank speeches.

text.p: The Bank for International Settlements (BIS) has expanded its web site on the Internet to include important statements and speeches on monetary policy by key central bankers.

So far the BIS site gives access to two recent statements; one by Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer on the Bundesbank's committment to stability and one by Bank of Japan governor Yasuo Matsushita on the role of monetary policy in Japan.

The plan is for key speeches on monetary policy to be available on the BIS web site within 24 hours of being given, much faster than now when economists and analysts have to wait for days until the full text of a speech arrives by mail.
The statements by Tietmeyer and Matsushita can also be found on the web sites of the Bundesbank and the Bank of Japan.

However, BIS is making the statements available through its own site to make it easier for central bank watchers to visit a single location to find the latest statements from central bank governors worldwide on national or global monetary policy.
BIS' web site -- http://www.bis.org -- went live last October and speeches by central bankers can be found by clicking on the newly-created section, BIS Review.
BIS, based in the Swiss city of Basle, is the worlds' oldest international financial institution and is owned and controlled by central banks.

Its main functions are to provide central banks with a forum for cooperation, to help central banks manage external reserves, to be a centre for monetary and economic research and to act as an agent for international financial agreements.
